newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: SOCCER-SAUDIS REACH FOURTH ASIAN CUP FINAL IN A ROW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SAUDIS REACH FOURTH ASIAN CUP FINAL IN A ROW.

text.p: Favourites Saudi Arabia beat Gulf rivals Iran 4-3 on penalties following a goalless draw after extra time on Wednesday to reach the Asian Cup final for a fourth consecutive time.
Saudi goalkeeper Mohammad Al Daeyea saved two spot kicks to put Saudi Arabia through for a showdown on Saturday with hosts the United Arab Emirates, who beat Kuwait 1-0 earlier on Wednesday.
Ahmed Madani struck the decisive penalty kick to silence the 15,000 Iranian supporters and send the Saudis celebrating.
Iran's substitute goalkeeper Ahmed Abedzadeh also saved two kicks but an earlier miss by top marksman Ali Daei cost the Iranian's the match.
Daei, the tournament's leading striker, missed the target with the first kick of the shoot-out to leave the field in tears.
The Saudis could have won the semifinal tie in the second half of normal time, hitting the bar twice.
A superb save from Iran's starting goalkeeper, Nima Nakisa, from a header by substitute Abdullah Al Dossary denied the Saudis a ''golden goal'' in the 24th minute of extra time.
Saudi Arabia won the title in 1984 and 1988 but lost to Japan in the final four years ago. Iran won the title three times back-to-back between 1968 and 1976.
After Saudi Arabia failed to make the most of early chances, Iran took charge and put their opponents under pressure for the remainder of the half.
Azizi and Daei combined well in one attack and it took a do-or-die tackle by the Saudi defence to deny Daei.
The Saudis began the second half in threatening mood, striker Fahad Al Mahalel rattling the crossbar with a fierce header from 15 metres after a cross by Jahani in the 62nd minute.
Saudi keeper Daeyea dived to his left to save brilliantly from a Daei header four minutes later.
Substitute Abdullah Al Dossary could have won it for Saudi Arabia in the last minute of normal time, but his ferocious shot from 25 metres hit the bar.

Iran: 22-Nima Nakisa (1-Ahmed Abedzadeh 117); 2-Naeim Sadavi; 4-Karim Bagheri; 5-Mohammad Ali ; 7-Ali Reza Mansourian (20-Darioush Yazdani 85); 9-Hamid Rezaestili; 10-Ali Daei; 11-Khodadad Azizi (12-Mahdi Mahdavikia 111); 14-Mohammad Khakpour; 18-Farshad Falahatzade; 25-Mehrdad Minavand.
